excerpt: In no event may the stated restricted period exceed 12 months from the date of cessation of employment, unless the employee has breached his or her fiduciary duty to the employer or the employee has unlawfully taken ... property ... in which case the duration may not exceed 2 years
note: 12-month statutory maximum; 2-year exception for fiduciary breach/unlawful taking.

note: Rebuttable presumption, not a hard cap. Also: ESHB 1155 (signed Mar 23, 2026) bans nearly all noncompetes effective June 30, 2027 (per law-firm alerts and the RCW page's future-effective version); in force as of Sept 2026 the 18-month presumption still applies.

excerpt: (G) Highly compensated employees (R. 2.2.11) $130,014 annually, and the EAP salary (row E) weekly ... Adopted as temporary rules on December 12, 2025; effective January 1, 2026

excerpt: (a) No employer shall enter into a covenant not to compete with any employee unless the employee's actual or expected annualized rate of earnings exceeds $75,000 per year. This amount shall increase to $80,000 per year beginning on January 1, 2027
note: Earnings must EXCEED $75,000 (strictly greater). Rises to $80,000 on Jan 1, 2027.

excerpt: No choice of law provision that would have the effect of avoiding the requirements of this section will be enforceable if the employee is, and has been for at least 30 days immediately preceding his or her cessation of employment, a resident of or employed in Massachusetts
note: G.L. c.149 §24L(e); limited to employees resident/employed in MA for 30 days before separation. Same subsection also fixes venue (county of residence or, by agreement, Suffolk).

excerpt: An employer must not require an employee who primarily resides and works in Minnesota, as a condition of employment, to agree to a provision ... that would ... (1) require the employee to adjudicate outside of Minnesota a claim arising in Minnesota; or (2) deprive the employee of the substantive protection of Minnesota law
note: Minn. Stat. 181.988 subd. 3; provision is voidable by the employee.

excerpt: 15.320 Specific types of contracts governed by Oregon law. Notwithstanding any other provision of ORS 15.300 to 15.380 ... the law of Oregon applies to the following contracts: ... (3) A contract of employment for services to be rendered primarily in Oregon by a resident of Oregon.
note: Not in the noncompete statute: ORS 653.295 has no choice-of-law or forum provision. The yes rests on the general contracts choice-of-law statute ORS 15.320(3), which overrides a foreign choice of law only for Oregon residents working primarily in Oregon (subject to ORS 15.305) and says nothing about forum. It overrides the clause rather than prohibiting the employer from requiring it. Borderline 'partly' if the question is read as requiring a noncompete-specific bar or a forum bar.

excerpt: At least 14 days before the individual commences employment for the employer; or ... at least 14 days before the employee must execute the agreement.
note: D.C. Code 32-581.03 (highly compensated employees only; ordinary non-competes are banned). Day type not specified (calendar by default).

excerpt: a copy of the noncompete agreement not less than 3 business days before the employer requires the agreement to be signed to allow time for the employee or prospective employee to review the agreement and negotiate
note: 26 M.R.S. 599-A(4); the employer must also disclose the requirement before the offer of employment.
